about: Small crescent rolls of tender cottage cheese and butter pastry, rolled around cinnamon sugar. Made with no yeast or baking powder.
title: Cottage cheese crescent rolls
skill: A soft cheese pastry with no leaven, rolled into crescents

notes.1: Makes 24 crescents. Bake them on two sheet pans, one at a time.
notes.2: Makes 48 crescents. Bake one pan at a time while you shape the next.

move.title: Pastry that puffs with no leaven
move.body: Mash butter and cottage cheese into flour for a soft dough, chill it, roll it out, and wrap wedges of it around cinnamon sugar. Steam from the butter and cheese gives the puff, not yeast.

why.title: Puffed, but unleavened
why.body: These rolls have no yeast and no baking powder, so they're good for the Feast of Unleavened Bread. They still puff a little: the water in the butter and the cottage cheese turns to steam in the oven and lifts the dough.

why.title: Why chill the dough
why.body: Soft butter makes a sticky dough that tears. An hour in the fridge firms the butter, so the dough rolls out smooth and holds its shape in the oven.

why.title: Roll from the wide end
why.body: Rolling each wedge from its wide end to its point wraps the filling inside and makes the crescent shape. Setting the point underneath keeps it from unrolling as it bakes.

wrong.sign: The dough is too sticky to roll
wrong.fix: Put it back in the fridge for 15 minutes, and dust the counter and rolling pin with flour.

wrong.sign: Filling is leaking out onto the pan
wrong.fix: Use a little less cinnamon sugar, and leave a bare edge at the wide end of each wedge.

wrong.sign: The bottoms are browning too fast
wrong.fix: Move the rack up one level, and check them a few minutes early.

quiz.q: With no yeast or baking powder, what makes these rolls puff?
choices: Steam from the butter and cheese
quiz.explain: The water in the butter and cottage cheese turns to steam in the hot oven and lifts the dough.

steps.text: Mash the cottage cheese and soft butter together in the large bowl with the fork, until only tiny lumps are left.
Stir in the flour and salt with the wooden spoon until a soft dough forms.
steps.tip: Don't taste the raw dough. Raw flour can make you sick.

steps.text: Divide the dough into pieces about the size of a baseball. Pat each into a flat disk, cover them, and put them in the fridge.
steps.tip: The dough can also chill overnight.

steps.text: Put a rack in the middle of the oven and heat it to 375°F. Line the sheet pan with parchment.
Stir the sugar and cinnamon together in the small bowl.
Dust the counter and rolling pin with flour. Roll one disk into a circle about 9 inches across. Sprinkle it evenly with cinnamon sugar.
Cut the circle into 6 wedges, like a pizza.
Roll each wedge up from the wide end to the point. Set them on the pan, point side down, about an inch apart.
Roll, fill, cut, and shape the rest of the dough the same way.
Bake one pan at a time, until golden.
steps.look: Golden brown on top, and deeper brown underneath.

steps.text: Move the crescents to the cooling rack with the spatula. Let them cool before eating.
steps.tip: The sugar inside stays very hot for a while.
